content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs line by line, building a full source ledger before concluding.

**Ledger highlights (all traced):**
- Core apparatus limitations (rigid base with first/second side, motor on first side, air-extraction mechanism on first side in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction perimeter loop/skirt of plastic/metal/PTFE or a combination of rigid materials, non-sealing restriction of inflow, continuous extraction keeping the chamber below atmosphere, differential holding without operator downforce, rigid-path low-damping transfer, free sliding while the vacuum maintains contact, guiding handles, rope/wire/cable pulling element, decoupled control) all trace to exact sentences in `input/disclosure.md`.
- Claim 10 / FIG. 6 / the stirring-element paragraph / the Field's "autonomously moving" trace to the single technical USER passage in `input/conversation.md` ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion", "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand", "already connected via vaccum"). The operational "resume/rebuild/tighten" USER turns were treated as non-disclosure.
- Background prior-art characterizations (`[REF:...]` passages) were excluded from inventor-support tracing per the instruction that a later review traces them to `prior_art/`.
- Depiction conventions stay inside the briefs: flat lower end of bearing face 26, ring width and plan form in FIG. 3, band depths in FIG. 4, block order/handle mounting in FIG. 1, cord meeting place in FIG. 5, stirring-element number/form/position in FIG. 6. No "by way of example" / "any closed outline" style broadening leaked into `04`–`10`; the application text keeps only permitted "shown schematically" recitals, and claims 8–10 stay location- and shape-neutral.
- Cross-checks: numerals 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48 each denote one part across briefs, description, and table; each figure's numeral list matches its callout list and the Brief Description's enumeration; section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are identical in FIG. 3's brief, FIG. 2/FIG. 4 view headers, and `07-drawings.md`; the FIG. 2 "in section / in elevation" enumeration now matches the FIG. 2 brief's hatched bodies; FIG. 2 (contact) and FIG. 4 (clearance) are reconciled by the "along at least part" limitation and FIG. 3's disclaimed angular section-line positions. No note, placeholder, question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains.

No findings to report.

input.summary: Complete ledger built and cleared. Every limitation of all twenty claims (independent 1, 11, 16 and dependents 2-10, 12-15, 17-20), all seventeen numbered parts (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48), all six figure briefs, the Brief Description of the Drawings, and every structure, material, relationship, result, operating condition and variant in the Field, Background, Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract were traced to affirmative inventor passages. The rigid base with first and second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) on the first side in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop/skirt of plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination of rigid materials, deliberate absence of an airtight seal, restriction of inflow, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, pressure-differential holding without operator downforce, rigid low-damping transmission path free of rubber/elastomer/foam, free sliding across areas while the vacuum maintains contact, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control all trace verbatim or near-verbatim to input/disclosure.md. Claim 10, the stirring-element paragraph, FIG. 6 and the Field's "autonomously moving" trace to the single technical USER passage ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion", "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand", "the device is already connected via vaccum"); the surrounding resume/rebuild/tighten USER turns were treated as operational and not as disclosure. Background prior-art characterizations bearing [REF:...] markers were excluded from inventor-support tracing per the standing instruction that a later review traces them to prior_art/. Depiction conventions remain confined to the figure briefs and add no undisclosed technical substance: the flat lower end of bearing face 26 and the enlarged clearance in FIG. 4, the ring width and rectangular plan form in FIG. 3, the schematic band depths and layer order in FIG. 4 (tile on bonding material on substrate, itself disclosed), the block order and handle mounting in FIG. 1, the schematic cord meeting place in FIG. 5, and the number, form and position of the stirring elements in FIG. 6; no shape, taper, angle, runout or contact-topology statement beyond the disclosed rigid bearing contact and the disclosed air path beneath the perimeter appears, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" style broadening leaked into the application text, whose claims and description stay shape- and location-neutral. Internal consistency verified: each numeral denotes one part across briefs, numeral table, claims and description; each figure's numeral list matches its callout list and the Brief Description enumeration; section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are repeated identically in the FIG. 3 brief, the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view headers and the drawing description; the FIG. 2 "shown in section / air-extraction mechanism in elevation" enumeration matches the FIG. 2 brief's hatched bodies and unhatched housing; and FIG. 2 showing contact while FIG. 4 shows the clearance is reconciled by the "along at least part of the perimeter member" limitation together with FIG. 3's disclaimed angular section-line positions. Claim antecedents, statutory classes and the "Not applicable." formalities from input/brief.md are consistent, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section or brief.
